facts.statement: The genus Oryctodromeus was described by Varricchio and colleagues in 2007.
facts.quote: authority: Varricchio et al., 2007

facts.statement: Oryctodromeus lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, specifically from the Albian to the Cenomanian ages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: 'mid'-Cretaceous(Albian–Cenomanian),

facts.statement: Fossils of Oryctodromeus have been found in the Blackleaf Formation of southwestern Montana and the Wayan Formation of southeastern Idaho, dating to roughly 105 to 96 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils are known from the mid-Cretaceous Blackleaf Formation of southwestern Montana and the Wayan Formation of southeastern Idaho, USA, both from around the Albian–Cenomanian ages, roughly 105-96 million years ago.

facts.statement: The name Oryctodromeus translates to "digger runner" based on Ancient Greek words for digger and runner.
facts.quote: Oryctodromeus (from Ancient Greek ὀρυκτήρ (oruktḗs), meaning "digger", and δρομαῖος (dromaîos), meaning "runner")

facts.statement: Oryctodromeus is a member of the family Thescelosauridae and is the first non-avian dinosaur to show published evidence of burrowing behavior.
facts.quote: A member of the small, presumably fast-running herbivorous family Thescelosauridae, Oryctodromeus is the first non-avian dinosaur published that shows evidence of burrowing behavior.

facts.statement: Adaptations in the jaws, forelimbs, and pelvis of Oryctodromeus could have helped it move and manipulate soil.
facts.quote: Adaptations in the jaws, forelimbs, and pelvis were described in the Blackleaf specimens that could have helped move and manipulate soil.

facts.statement: Additional fossils from the Wayan Formation show further adaptations for digging located in the femur.
facts.quote: Additional material from the Wayan Formation demonstrates further adaptations for digging in the femur.

facts.statement: The type specimen MOR 1636a is a partial adult skeleton including the premaxillae, part of the braincase, vertebrae from the neck, back, hip, and tail, ribs, shoulder girdle, an arm without a hand, tibiae, an incomplete fibula, and a metatarsal.
facts.quote: Oryctodromeus is based on specimens from the Blackleaf Formation: MOR 1636a, a partial skeleton of an adult individual including: the premaxillae (upper beak); part of the braincase; three neck, six back, seven hip, and twenty-three tail vertebrae; ribs; the shoulder girdle; an arm (minus the hand); both tibiae and an incomplete fibula; and a metatarsal.

facts.statement: Two juvenile individuals, designated MOR 1636b, are about 55 to 65% the size of the adult type specimen.
facts.quote: Two additional individuals, both juveniles about 55 to 65% the size of MOR 1636a, are represented by MOR 1636b.

facts.statement: In 2023, Oryctodromeus was designated as the state dinosaur of Idaho.
facts.quote: In 2023, Oryctodromeus was designated as the state dinosaur of Idaho, in which many of its fossils have been recovered.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Oryctodromeus as basal within Euornithopoda and close to the hypsilophodonts Orodromeus and Zephyrosaurus.
facts.quote: Under a cladistic analysis, Oryctodromeus was found to be basal within Euornithopoda and a close relative of the hypsilophodonts Orodromeus and Zephyrosaurus, which are also known from the Cretaceous of Montana.

facts.statement: Adult Oryctodromeus measured 2.1 meters long and weighed between 22 and 32 kilograms, while juveniles were about 1.3 meters long.
facts.quote: The adult Oryctodromeus itself measured 2.1 m long and would have weighed about 22-32 kilograms (50-70 pounds), and the juveniles would have been about 1.3 m long.

facts.statement: The presence of juveniles with adults suggests parental care, indicating that rearing young was at least one motivation for burrowing.
facts.quote: The presence of juveniles with the adult suggests parental care, and that at least one motivation for burrowing was to rear the juveniles.

facts.statement: Three Oryctodromeus individuals were found buried in an underground burrow measuring about 2 meters long and 70 centimeters wide.
facts.quote: The three Oryctodromeus individuals were found buried within the remains of an underground den or burrow that measured about 2 m long and 70 cm wide.

facts.statement: The preserved burrow section contains two turns and smaller secondary cylinders likely made by smaller commensal animals sharing the burrow.
facts.quote: There are two turns in the preserved burrow section, and smaller secondary sandstone cylinders of various sizes (a few centimeters or inches in cross-section at most) that were probably made by smaller animals sharing the burrow (commensal).

facts.statement: Oryctodromeus belongs to the family Thescelosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Thescelosauridae

facts.statement: The genus authority for Oryctodromeus is Varricchio et al., 2007.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Varricchio et al., 2007

facts.statement: Oryctodromeus existed in the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que existieron a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 95 millones de años, en el Cenomaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: As a bipedal runner like other hypsilophodonts, Oryctodromeus reached nearly 2.1 meters in length and 70 centimeters in height, while juveniles were around 1.3 meters long.
facts.quote: Como todos los hipsilofodóntidos fue un pequeño corredor bípedo, que llegó a medir cerca de los 2,1 metros de longitud y 70 centímetros de altura, los juveniles medían alrededor de 1,3 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Specimens from the Wayan Formation show a thick tendon network in the dorsal, sacral, and caudal columns, perhaps indicating more flexibility in ossified tendons than previously supposed.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los especímenes de la Formación Wayan demuestran la presencia de una gruesa red de tendones en las columnas dorsales, sacras y caudales de algunos especímenes, quizás indicando más flexibilidad en los tendones osificados de lo que se suponía anteriormente.

facts.statement: This is the first studied dinosaur showing evidence of living in burrows, a trait combined with its cursorial nature that gave the species its name, translating to "lair-digging runner".
facts.quote: Este es el primer dinosaurio estudiado que exhibe evidencia de haber habitado en madrigueras, este aspecto con el hecho de su aspecto de animal cursorial le dio el nombre a la especie Oryctodromeus cubicularis que se traduce como el "corredor excavador de la madriguera".

facts.statement: Oryctodromeus belongs to the subfamily Orodrominae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Orodrominae

facts.statement: The genus Oryctodromeus is classified within the family Thescelosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Thescelosauridae

facts.statement: Oryctodromeus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Oryctodromeus lived between 106.3 and 93.9 million years ago during the Albian to Cenomanian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Cenomanian (106.3 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis revealed that Oryctodromeus was basal within Euornithopoda.
facts.quote: por medio de un análisis cladista, se descubrió que el Oryctodromeus era basal dentro de Euornithopoda

facts.statement: Oryctodromeus shared adaptations such as a wide snout with Orodromeus and Zephyrosaurus that may have been used for digging.
facts.quote: Estos dos animales comparten adaptaciones con Oryctodromeus que pueden haber sido utilizados para excavar, como un hocico ancho.

facts.statement: Three individuals of Oryctodromeus were found buried within the remains of a subterranean burrow measuring approximately 2 meters long and 70 centimeters wide.
facts.quote: Los tres individuos de Oryctodromeus fueron encontrados enterrados dentro de los restos de una madriguera subterránea, que mide aproximadamente 2 metros de largo y 70 centímetros de ancho.

facts.statement: The skeletons were densely packed and disarticulated, indicating the animals died and decomposed inside the burrow.
facts.quote: Los esqueletos estaban densamente empaquetados y desarticulados, lo que indica que los animales murieron y se pudrieron dentro de la madriguera.

facts.statement: The burrow is similar to those made today by hyenas and aardwolves.
facts.quote: La madriguera es similar a las hechas hoy por hienas y frailecillos.

facts.statement: The burrow was filled with sand, resulting in sandstone that stands out against the surrounding mudstone and clay.
facts.quote: Estaba lleno de arena , y la piedra arenisca resultante se destaca contra la piedra de barro y arcilla de los alrededores .

facts.statement: The preserved burrow section has two turns and smaller secondary sandstone cylinders up to a few centimeters in cross-section, likely made by smaller animals sharing the burrow.
facts.quote: Hay dos vueltas en la sección de la madriguera preservada, y cilindros de arenisca secundaria más pequeños de varios tamaños, unos pocos centímetrosde sección transversal como máximo, que probablemente fueron hechos por animales más pequeños que comparten la madriguera.

facts.statement: The burrow fits well with the probable proportions of an adult dinosaur, providing further evidence that Oryctodromeus was the burrower.
facts.quote: La madriguera se ajusta mucho a las proporciones probables del dinosaurio adulto, otra indicación de que era el cavador.

facts.statement: Robert Bakker has informally claimed since the 1990s that the Jurassic dinosaur Drinker lived in burrows, but this has not yet been published.
facts.quote: Robert Bakker ha afirmado informalmente desde la década de 1990 que Drinker, del Jurásico tardío de Wyoming, vivía en madrigueras, pero esto aún no se ha publicado.
